text:
mike: Hey all — seeing a gap in traces for kafka-consumer. Producer spans are visible in Tempo but the consumer side only has logs, no child spans. Anyone seen span loss across Kafka headers?

sara: Which environment and a sample trace id? Link helps.

mike: prod-east. Trace id 8f3a2b1c4d5e6f7a. Link: https://observability.internal/tempo/trace/8f3a2b1c4d5e6f7a

mike: Logs show message processed and business logic ran, but no consumer spans in the trace.

devon: Common culprits: sampling mismatch, header propagation, collector/exporter errors, or the consumer library reserializing messages and dropping headers. What language + client lib?

mike: Go service using sarama + our wrapper. We use otel-go auto-instrumentation (otel/sdk@v1.19) and otel-instrumentation-kafka. Sampling global set to 0.1. Not sure why producer spans appear but consumer doesn't.

clara: Quick checks: verify headers are preserved in Kafka. Use kafka-console-consumer with --property print.headers=true or curl the broker. Also grep consumer logs for "traceparent".

mike: Ran console consumer, headers are present: traceparent: 00-8f3a2b1c4d5e6f7a...-01, so the broker keeps headers.

sara: If headers survive, next check is the consumer extraction. Are you creating new records or using a framework that loses headers when converting to internal event type? Also ensure propagators are configured (TraceContext).

devon: Right — also the W3C sampled flag matters. If producer sampled=false, downstream won't create child spans. But you said producer spans exist, so likely sampled=true.

mike: I enabled OTEL_LOG_LEVEL=debug on the consumer and saw: \"failed to marshal span: unsupported attribute type\" from the OTLP exporter. Could that drop spans locally?

clara: Yes — exporter/collector errors can cause spans to be dropped. That log points to an attribute you set that OTLP can't encode (e.g., []byte or complex struct). Check attributes you're attaching to spans/attributes on the message.

mike: We were attaching the raw Kafka message key ([]byte) as an attribute. Changed to base64 string and restarted.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Finished canary rollout to prod-east for kafka-consumer v1.4.7 :white_check_mark:

mike: After the change I can see consumer spans linked to the same trace in Tempo. Looks fixed.

sara: Nice. Can you open a quick PR to sanitize attributes (no []byte/structs) and add a unit test + note in runbook? I'll review.

mike: Will do. Also adding a ticket to add a linter to prevent non-serializable span attributes.

devon: For the runbook, add a short checklist: header check, propagators, sampling flags, collector/exporter logs, attribute types, and a quick reproduction (SAMPLE_RATE=1 run locally). Example extraction snippet to include:

```go
// consumer handler (example)
msg := <sarama.ConsumerMessage>
ctx := context.Background()
// convert headers to a map[string]string
headers := headersToMap(msg.Headers)
ctx = otel.GetTextMapPropagator().Extract(ctx, propagation.MapCarrier(headers))
tr := otel.Tracer("kafka-consumer")
ctx, span := tr.Start(ctx, "kafka.process")
defer span.End()
// process
```

clara: Great, this will help others. Marking this resolved. :thumbsup:

mike: Thanks everyone!
